subject: School Lunch Price Increase
overview: The Committee approved the first school lunch price increase in ten years to meet federal compliance and adopted a revised head lice policy based on contemporary medical guidance. They also received reports on district-wide upgrades to facility infrastructure, student information software, and phone systems.

items.title: Routine Business
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes from June 1 and the budget hearing, as well as bills, transfer of funds, and payrolls.

items.title: Nobel Laureate Presentation
items.summary: Rocco Cieri reported on a visit from Nobel Laureate Jerome Friedman, who toured the renovated Medford High School science facilities and lectured students on particle physics.

items.title: Capital Improvements Update
items.summary: The district reviewed ongoing and emergency capital repairs from FY15, including new water heaters at Roberts and Columbus Schools and boiler work at the high school.

items.title: Student Information System Transition
items.summary: The committee reviewed a recommendation to replace the decertified I-PASS system with 'School Brains' to ensure state data compliance and provide a more robust parent portal.

items.title: District Phone System Report
items.summary: Staff presented options for replacing failing telephone infrastructure with potential VoIP or Centrex services, prioritizing the Brooks and McGlynn schools for initial implementation.

items.title: Food Service Price Increase
items.summary: Approved a mid-range price increase for school lunches to comply with federal USDA equity mandates and build reserves for aging kitchen equipment.

items.title: Head Lice Policy Revision
items.summary: Adopted a revised health policy shifting from 'no-nit' exclusion to a screening and education model designed to minimize student absences.

items.title: Summer Rules and Executive Session
items.summary: Approved operating rules for the summer months and entered executive session to discuss collective bargaining for custodial and teacher unions.
